**Finding submitted: deviation (MINCOMMIT), confidence 0.95.**

**What I found**
- § 2.1 (p0012) is the only clause imposing a purchase commitment on us: USD 2,000,000 per year for three years, on a take-or-pay basis, "without reduction or termination rights." That is a multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction or exit — the playbook's walk-away scenario, and it fails every fallback element (12-month scope, 30-day reduction right, true-up instead of penalty).
- § 12.3 (p0044) directly contradicts it ("Customer has made no ... minimum-volume ... commitment"), and § 7.1 (p0025) already limits us to Fees stated in each Order Form and bars unidentified minimum-use charges — so the commitment is both one-sided and internally inconsistent.
- Other hits are not responsive: the "shortfall" references in §§ 22.2–22.3 relate to audited licence underpayments, and § 7.1's "minimum-use" language is a restriction on Vendor (in our favour), so neither is flagged.

**Change proposed (validated, ok:true)**
One surgical replacement of the § 2.1 sentence with the preferred position: "Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment and pays only for usage or Services ordered under an Order Form." This removes the take-or-pay, cures the § 12.3 conflict, and leaves the rest of Section 2 untouched; the fallback (12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up not penalty) is offered in the comment if Vendor needs some commitment.
